A2.title: Group() helper for named contexts
A2.problem: Commands must call Slog().WithGroup("name") and lose the typed *Logger surface (Errorf unavailable on grouped loggers).
A2.proposal: Add Logger.Group(name string) *Logger that wraps inner.WithGroup(name).

notes: One-liner: return &Logger{inner: l.inner.WithGroup(name)}
Child logger owns no resources (closers empty), same contract as With()
Migrate call sites in internal/infra/commands/cmd_process.go:62 and :91 to drop the Slog() escape hatch

benefits: Preserves typed surface (*Logger not *slog.Logger)
Consistent with With() API
Removes boilerplate in commands
trade_offs: Another method to remember
tests: TestLogger_Group returns a different instance and logs grouped output
Errorf available on grouped child logger
A2.outcome: Implemented with interface port: pipeline.Logger interface in internal/app/pipeline/dto.go (Debug/Info/Warn/Error; both *slog.Logger and *logging.Logger satisfy it). cmd_process.go fully migrated off Slog(); pipeline.Options.Logger is now the interface.

A3.title: JSON vs text format toggle
A3.problem: Terminal output is always JSON (machine-readable but unreadable for humans).
A3.proposal: Add optional format field to [logger] config: "json" (default) or "text".

notes: newTermHandler switches on strings.EqualFold(cfg.Format, "text"): text -> slog.NewTextHandler(os.Stderr, opts), default -> slog.NewJSONHandler
File handler stays JSON (machine-consumed)
Empty format defaults to "json" — no breaking change

benefits: Humans get readable terminal logs
No breaking changes (default json)
trade_offs: One extra config field
Text output less structured
tests: TestNewTermHandler_FormatText — text format writes non-JSON lines
TestNewTermHandler_FormatJSON — format "json" and "" keep JSON output
TestNewTermHandler_FormatCaseInsensitive — "TEXT" accepted
TestNewTermHandler_NoTerminal — nil handler when Terminal=false
TestNewLogger_TerminalTextFormat — end-to-end NewLogger with text format
A3.outcome: Implemented. config.Logging gained Format field; newTermHandler switches Text/JSON (case-insensitive "text"); file handler unchanged. Terminal-only tests capture os.Stderr via pipe.

A4.title: Color support for terminal logs
A4.problem: Human-readable text logs are colorless; levels don't stand out.
A4.proposal: Add optional color field to [logger] config; colorize level values in terminal text output.

notes: ReplaceAttr approach from the proposal does NOT work: TextHandler quotes values containing control characters via strconv.Quote, so ANSI escapes would be emitted as literal \x1b text
Implemented colorLevelWriter — an io.Writer wrapper around os.Stderr that colorizes the level field of each line (TextHandler guarantees one Write per record)
Colors DEBUG=cyan INFO=green WARN=yellow ERROR=red with reset after level token
Only effective when format = "text"; JSON output ignored
No new dependency — raw ANSI escapes
Colors apply to terminal handler only — file output stays plain
No TTY detection: color=true is an explicit opt-in; keep the zero-value default false

benefits: Levels scannable at a glance in text mode
trade_offs: No TTY detection — color=true writes escapes even when stderr is redirected
Colors not copied to file
Writer-level colorizer depends on TextHandler line format (time=... level=...)
tests: TestNewTermHandler_ColorText — color=true text mode emits ANSI-escaped level (level=\x1b[32mINFO\x1b[0m)
TestNewTermHandler_ColorDisabled — color=false text mode emits no escapes
TestNewTermHandler_ColorJSONIgnored — color=true json mode emits no escapes
A4.outcome: Implemented. config.Logging gained Color field; newTermHandler wraps os.Stderr in colorLevelWriter when format=text and color=true. ReplaceAttr was rejected: TextHandler escapes control chars via strconv.Quote, so ANSI codes cannot pass through the value pipeline. File and JSON output stay plain.

C1.title: Config package refactoring
C1.problem: defaultCFG() had weak defaults: logger.path was the placeholder "/path/to/file" (file handler tried to open this bogus path on every run) and the executor map was empty (all 6 runtime keys silently fell back to the generator output root, giving no hint they exist).
C1.proposal: Clean up the config package after A4 settles the Logging struct: fix placeholder defaults and make executor keys discoverable.

notes: Logger.Path default "/path/to/file" -> "" (empty disables file logging, already supported by newFileHandler)

Seed defaultCFG executor map with the 6 runtime keys (target, buffer, in_progress, done, notifications, archive) using the same fallback values buildScriptConfig computes, so a generated config documents them
Add Validate() (configmanager.Validator hook) for logger.level whitelisting and non-empty generator paths
Re-check struct shape after A4 adds Color — do not start before A4 is done

benefits: Freshly generated config no longer attempts to write /path/to/file
Executor keys self-documenting in generated config
Load-time validation catches bad logger.level early instead of silently coercing to info
trade_offs: Seeded executor defaults duplicate fallback logic in buildScriptConfig
Validate() adds a failure mode for configs that previously loaded with warnings
tests: TestDefaultConfig_LoggerPath — default Logger.Path is "/path/to/file.log"
TestDefaultConfig_ExecutorMapSeeded — default map contains all 6 keys
TestDefaultConfig_PassesValidation — default passes Validate
TestConfig_ValidateBadLevel — invalid logger.level rejected
TestConfig_ValidateEmptyGeneratorPath — empty generator paths rejected
TestLoad_ValidateRejectsBadLevel — invalid logger.level fails Load (HOME-isolated)
TestLoad_ValidateRejectsEmptyGeneratorPath — empty generator path fails Load (HOME-isolated)
Existing TestDefaultConfig_LoggerPath replaced by TestDefaultConfig_LoggerPathEmpty
Existing TestDefaultConfig_ExecutorMap replaced by TestDefaultConfig_ExecutorMapSeeded
C1.outcome: Logger.Path fixed to "" (no file handler on fresh config). Executor map seeded with 6 keys mirroring buildScriptConfig fallbacks (target→root/target, buffer/in_progress/done/notifications→root, archive→root/archive). Validate() added: logger.level whitelist (debug/info/warn/error), generator input/output/metadata non-empty. Note: DiscoverAndLoad swallows validation errors and falls through to ~/.config — an invalid explicit config silently loads the user's real config. This is a configmanager library behavior; not in scope to fix. Observation: Storage.Path still has "/path/to/file.json" placeholder (same class as Logger.Path, out of scope for C1).

A5.title: Custom slog text handler with format template
A5.problem: slog.TextHandler has no format customization options — field order, separators, timestamp format, and structure are all fixed.
A5.proposal: Replace slog.TextHandler with a custom handler that renders a format string like '{time} [{level}] {msg} {attrs}'. Minimal template set: {time}, {level}, {msg}, {attrs}. colorLevelWriter post-processing continues to work on the writer.

notes: Implement slog.Handler interface with template parsing
WithAttrs accumulates attrs; WithGroup adds key prefix
Enabled compares level; Handle renders template against Record
colorLevelWriter wraps os.Stderr as before — post-processing on raw bytes
File handler stays JSON (unaffected)

benefits: Full control over terminal text output format
Field order, separators, quoting customizable
No new dependencies
trade_offs: Replaces slog.TextHandler entirely — lose upstream improvements
Template parsing per log record (minor overhead)
Basic template (no conditionals, no per-field formatting)

S1.title: Config struct refactor: ScriptGeneration block
S1.source: internal/infra/config/config.go — Hardsub is a standalone top-level struct, hard to extend
S1.problem: Hardsub is a standalone top-level struct in Config. Script-generation settings (hardsub tag, ffmpeg binary, future filter presets) are scattered across the config with no natural grouping. This makes the config hard to extend and harder for users to understand what settings belong together.
S1.proposal: Introduce a ScriptGeneration config block that groups all script-generation settings. Move Hardsub into it, add FfmpegBinary field. This is iterative: start with Hardsub + FfmpegBinary, add more fields as needed.

implementation.config_change: New ScriptGeneration struct with Hardsub (moved from top-level) and FfmpegBinary string. Config struct gains ScriptGeneration field; Hardsub field removed from top-level.
implementation.migration: TOML key [script_generation] with nested hardsub { tag } and ffmpeg_binary. Backwards compat: [hardsub] still reads into ScriptGeneration.Hardsub for existing configs.
notes: New ScriptGeneration { Hardsub Hardsub; FfmpegBinary string } struct
Move Hardsub from top-level into ScriptGeneration
Add FfmpegBinary string field (currently hardcoded in template.go:43)
Backwards compat: [hardsub] TOML section still populates ScriptGeneration.Hardsub
Update defaultCFG: ScriptGeneration.Hardsub.Tag = "Forsirovannye", FfmpegBinary = "ffmpeg"
Update all config accessors: cfg.Hardsub.Tag → cfg.ScriptGeneration.Hardsub.Tag
Update pipeline options to read from ScriptGeneration

benefits: All script-generation settings grouped under one config block
Easy to add more settings (frame rate, preset, filter options) without touching top-level
Clearer config structure for users
Prepares for S2: ffmpeg binary configurability
trade_offs: Breaking change for existing config files (need [hardsub] → [script_generation.hardsub] migration)
Backwards compat key adds slight complexity
All config accessors need updating (cfg.Hardsub → cfg.ScriptGeneration.Hardsub)
tests: TestScriptGeneration_HardsubTag — default tag preserved
TestScriptGeneration_FfmpegBinary — default is "ffmpeg"
TestScriptGeneration_TOMLNewFormat — [script_generation] section parsed correctly
TestDefaultConfig_ScriptGeneration — defaultCFG has non-empty ScriptGeneration
S1.outcome: Implemented. Config struct gained ScriptGeneration block with Hardsub (moved from top-level) and FfmpegBinary string. All accessors updated: cfg.Hardsub.Tag → cfg.ScriptGeneration.Hardsub.Tag. TOML format changed from [hardsub] to [script_generation.hardsub]. Breaking change: existing config files with [hardsub] section must migrate to [script_generation.hardsub]. Tests cover defaults, TOML new format, and backward compat note removed (no backward compat needed).

S2.title: Make ffmpeg binary configurable via app configuration
S2.problem: ffmpeg binary path is hardcoded in internal/domain/script/template.go:43: `` ffmpeg -n -r 25 -i ... ``. Users cannot specify a custom ffmpeg binary (e.g., /opt/bin/ffmpeg, or a wrapper). ffprobe IS configurable (paths.generator.ffprobe_binary), but ffmpeg (used in generated scripts) is not.
S2.proposal: Pass ffmpeg binary path from config through pipeline → ScriptConfig → template placeholder. Template uses |=ffmpeg_binary=| placeholder replaced by buildScriptConfig with the configured value (or fallback to "ffmpeg").

implementation.dataflow: config → Pipeline.Options.FfmpegBinary → buildScriptConfig → ScriptConfig.FfmpegBinary → template placeholder |=ffmpeg_binary=| → replaced in generated .sh script
notes: Add FfmpegBinary string to Pipeline.Options (dto.go)
Add FfmpegBinary string to ScriptConfig (config.go)
Add |=ffmpeg_binary=| placeholder to AmediaGeneric template (template.go)
Replace placeholder in buildScriptConfig with configured path (config.go)
Pipeline passes FfmpegBinary from config to buildScriptConfig
Fallback: "ffmpeg" if not configured (same as ffprobe default)

benefits: Users can specify custom ffmpeg binary path (e.g., /opt/bin/ffmpeg, nvidia-enabled build)
Consistent with ffprobe configurability (both binaries now config-driven)
Generated scripts use the correct ffmpeg binary
trade_offs: Touches domain layer (ScriptConfig) — adds one field
Template placeholder adds one line to the template
Pipeline dataflow change: ffmpeg binary must flow from config through pipeline to script builder
tests: TestBuildScriptConfig_FfmpegBinary — custom ffmpeg path appears in generated script
TestBuildScriptConfig_FfmpegBinaryFallback — default "ffmpeg" used when not configured
TestBuildScriptConfig_FfmpegBinaryEmpty — empty string falls back to "ffmpeg"
TestTemplate_FfmpegPlaceholder — |=ffmpeg_binary=| replaced in rendered template
S2.outcome: Implemented. ScriptConfig gained FfmpegBinary field; template replaced hardcoded ffmpeg with |=ffmpeg_binary=| placeholder; BuildScript falls back to 'ffmpeg' when empty; Pipeline.Options gained FfmpegBinary; buildScriptConfig passes it through; cmd_process.go wires cfg.ScriptGeneration.FfmpegBinary with nonEmpty fallback. Tests added: TestBuildScript_FfmpegBinary, TestBuildScript_FfmpegBinaryFallback, TestBuildScriptConfig_FfmpegBinary, TestBuildScriptConfig_FfmpegBinaryFallback, TestBuildScriptConfig_FfmpegBinaryEmpty.

D1.title: Default configuration refactoring
D1.source: User request: the default configuration must let the user start working immediately and must tell which fields to fill in
D1.problem: The built-in default configuration does not let the user start working immediately and, most importantly, the user does not know which fields in the configuration are available. Default values look like usable paths (/tmp/lazyam3/input) or dummy placeholders (/path/to/file.log), so a fresh setup silently runs with unusable settings and gives no guidance.
D1.proposal: Refactor the default configuration into self-documenting placeholder values and fail fast with a message pointing to the config file when the effective configuration equals the built-in default.

notes: Replace defaultCFG() placeholder values with self-documenting placeholders (e.g. /path/to/lazyam3/input)
Detect effective config equal to defaultCFG() and return a default-configuration error
Error message must include the config file path the user has to edit and the required fields

benefits: User immediately understands which fields to fill in the default config
Startup fails fast with an actionable message instead of running on unusable defaults
No silent misconfiguration on fresh installs
trade_offs: Default configuration is no longer directly usable — the user must always create or edit a config file
Equality-based detection also flags user configs that intentionally mirror the defaults
tests: TestDefaultConfig_ContainsPlaceholders — defaults are self-documenting
TestIsDefault — detects effective config equal to the built-in default
TestLoad_DefaultConfigDetected — fresh install without a config file returns the default-config error
TestLoad_UserConfigNotDefault — user-edited config loads normally
TestLoad_ExplicitConfigEqualToDefault — explicit config equal to the default returns the default-config error
D1.outcome: Implemented. defaultCFG() now returns self-documenting placeholders (/path/to/lazyam3/input, /path/to/lazyam3/output, /path/to/lazyam3/metadata.json, /path/to/lazyam3/storage.json, /path/to/lazyam3/lazyam3.log, executor mirrors /path/to/lazyam3/output). Config gained IsDefault() (reflect.DeepEqual vs defaultCFG()) and typed *DefaultConfigError (wraps ErrDefaultConfig, carries ConfigPath). Load() returns the default-config error when the effective config equals the default; AppModules.Init fails fast before the pipeline is created. Fresh install terminates with: 'default configuration in use: edit the config file "<path>" and fill in the required fields (paths.generator.input_directory, paths.generator.output_directory, paths.generator.metadata_path) to enable processing'. Trade-offs accepted: default config is no longer directly usable; equality-based detection also flags user configs that intentionally mirror the defaults.

S3.title: Configurable hardsub parameters
S3.source: User request: all parameters we are using in the script template for hardsub are worthy to be configurable
S3.problem: Hardsub burn-in in the generated ffmpeg script hardcodes subtitles filter parameters such as font, colours and margins in BuildScript; users cannot tune burn-in behaviour.
S3.proposal: Make all hardsub parameters used in the script template configurable via the config, for example under script_generation.hardsub.

notes: Move hardcoded subtitles filter arguments from buildHSUB into config-driven parameters
Extend Harsub struct or add nested parameter structs as fields are added

benefits: Hardsub burn-in behaviour tunable without code changes
All script-template hardsub parameters become user-configurable
trade_offs: More config fields to keep in sync with the script template
Default values needed for IsDefault equality detection

TestBuildScript_HardsubParametersFallback — defaults used when not configured

S4.title: Configurable script generation command parameters
S4.source: User request: same as Harsub, add more structs: GlobalParameters, VideoStream, AudioStream — all of them can contain individual repeatable parameters
S4.problem: ffmpeg command construction in the generated script such as binary, rate, filter_complex and output options is assembled in code; users cannot add custom command parameters.
S4.proposal: Group script-generation command parameters into GlobalParameters, VideoStream and AudioStream structs, each holding individual repeatable parameters.

notes: GlobalParameters: global ffmpeg options such as binary and rate
VideoStream: per-stream filters and options

Repeatable parameters via slices

benefits: Users can tune ffmpeg commands without code changes
Repeatable per-stream parameters
trade_offs: Larger config surface and validation burden
Template placeholders for new parameters needed
